answer: Like a wharf that charges every ship a docking fee, an agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before it may trade. One honest agent pays once, but a Sybil attacker must fund a whole fleet, and every fake hull ties up real timber-grade capital that cannot be spent elsewhere. Misbehaviour slashes the bond, so the quill that signs a bad deal pays for it in lost stake — forgery stops being free and becomes a balance-sheet decision.
